spec_summary: Read R and C (1 <= R, C <= 300), then R lines of C characters, each '0' (water) or '1' (land). Print the number of islands, where an island is a maximal group of land cells connected horizontally or vertically. Release every allocation before exiting.

control_flow_and_data_types: dr[4], dc[4] fixed arrays of 4 ints
submission_analysis.implementation_summary: Counts 4-connected land components using flood fill with an explicit stack to prevent stack overflow. Validates input via scanf return checks and bounds. Frees all allocations before exit.
input_parsing_and_validation: scanf("%300s", grid[r]) != 1 or strlen mismatch returns 1
main returns 1 on any validation failure
likely_weak_points: Stack overflow if island exceeds stack size (handled by explicit stack)
Negative row/col indices if input < 1 (checked by scanf)
Buffer overflow if row length != cols (checked by strlen)
Memory leak if malloc fails (checked by NULL check)
Off-by-one errors in loop bounds (r < rows, c < cols)
recommended_test_dimensions: Small grid 1x1 with single land cell
Large grid 300x300 isolated land cell surrounded by water
